cases.description: Envelope C with its artifact octets replaced after signing. artifact_digest FAIL, so anchor_inclusion is never run (§6.2.1 step 4); §8.1 row 2.
A validly signed envelope for request C that binds the digest of another request. request_binding FAIL; §8.1 row 2.

Envelope C naming the trusted responder key, signed by another key. envelope_signature FAIL, so anchor_inclusion is never run (§6.2.1 step 4); §8.1 row 2. responder_trust checks the named key and passes (reading P-54).
Envelope C signed by, and naming, a key the trust policy does not accept. responder_trust FAIL; §8.1 row 2. The material still proves the artifact (§6.2.1 step 4 does not depend on trust).
A request for another record, answered with envelope C's subject. subject_binding FAIL; §8.1 row 2.
A request pinning another checkpoint, answered under §10.1's checkpoint. anchor_match FAIL; §8.1 row 2. The material proves the artifact under the checkpoint the envelope names.
Envelope C with one octet of its inclusion proof changed in transit. verification_binding FAIL, so anchor_inclusion is never run (§6.2.1 step 4); §8.1 row 2 (§10.1, last paragraph).
The changed inclusion proof, with the envelope re-signed over its digest. The material is bound, and does not prove the artifact: anchor_inclusion FAIL at §6.2.1 step 12; §8.1 row 2.
A refusal that verifies under its own key_id, a key the trust policy does not accept. responder_trust FAIL: a response received and failed, UNKNOWN; never a refusal outcome.
A refusal naming the trusted responder key, signed by another key. refusal_signature FAIL; UNKNOWN. responder_trust checks the named key against the policy and passes (reading P-54).
A conforming refusal with reason policy_declined. WITHHELD, which projects to GAP; the claim's carrier is analysis or story, never disclosure.
A conforming refusal with reason no_such_subject: evidence not found. NOT_FOUND, projecting to GAP.
Nothing arrived for request C within its one-minute window. The requester's absence record maps to UNKNOWN, never to a refusal; the claim SHOULD use story.

The absence record of missing-evidence-recorded-absence, signed by the requester. The signing input is JCS of every member except sig, key_id included (§6.4). Conforming; the same UNKNOWN as the unsigned record.

The same absence record, signed over every member except key_id and sig: the refusal's signing input (§6.3), not the absence record's (§6.4). The signature does not verify, so the record is not a conforming absence and no claim is made from it.
The same absence record with key_id and no sig. key_id and sig are both present or both absent (§6.4), so the record is not a conforming absence and no claim is made from it.

The same absence record with the valid sig of missing-evidence-recorded-absence-signed and no key_id. key_id and sig are both present or both absent (§6.4), so the record is not a conforming absence and no claim is made from it.

Request C asks for evidence-interop/0; the envelope names evidence-interop/1. The verifier implements both, so only the mismatch rule of §3.3 step 5 applies: profile_version FAIL and every other envelope property NOT_CHECKED; §8.1 row 2.
An artifact response with no profile member, as from a responder implementing the Evidence Request draft alone. profile_version NOT_PRESENT; §8.1 row 3.

A request and envelope under evidence-interop/1, checked by a verifier that implements only evidence-interop/0. profile_version NOT_CHECKED, every other property NOT_CHECKED, never checked under v0 rules; §8.1 row 4.
A request naming evidence-interop/9, which the responder does not implement. It refuses with request_malformed (§3.3 step 4); a conforming refusal, UNKNOWN.

Every envelope property PASS; the carried JWS fails its own signature check. The requirement that IS the check is SATISFIED and not_met (row 5); the one the check only SUPPORTS is INSUFFICIENT (row 6).

cases.description: A proposal and an execution record, and no answer from the acceptor. No candidate: not_accepted, and the requirements are the requester's own expectations.
§11.1.9 A: an acceptance written after the action, dated before it, with no ordering evidence. It must not reach accepted_before_action.
§11.1.9 B: a receipt signed by the acceptor itself does not count as ordering evidence.
§11.1.9 C: an honest receipt from the proposer, received after the action. It counts, and its ordering point is not earlier than the action: INCONCLUSIVE.
§11.1.9 D: an accepted record whose own issued_at is after the action. The acceptor's own record admits it: acceptance_ordering FAIL, accepted_after_action.
§11.1.9 E: the same record bytes as A, with a proposer's receipt received before the action. PASS, accepted_before_action.
§11.1.9 F: the trust policy maps the proposer key to the acceptor's party. Neither key is accepted in its role: not_accepted.
§11.1.9 G: the inputs of E, while the action truly took place at 00:01. The true time is not an input, so the result is E's: the limit of §11.1.10.
§11.1.9 G under a trust policy requiring a time for the action from a party other than the acceptor: none is held, so acceptance_ordering is NOT_PRESENT (§11.1.5 rule 3).
§11.2.7 A: N supersedes I's record. lifecycle_not_issuer; no effect.
§11.2.7 B, control: I supersedes its own record.
§11.2.7 C: issuer names I, the signature is N's. lifecycle_signature FAIL; the issuer is not established.
§11.2.7 D: S_N and S_I, in either order. Only S_I qualifies, so it is unique.
§11.2.7 D in the other order of receipt: the same findings and state.
§11.2.7 E: N amends I's record. lifecycle_not_issuer.
§11.2.7 F: I2, mapped to I's party but not a successor, supersedes. lifecycle_not_issuer.
§11.2.7 G: the trust policy states that I2 succeeds I.
§11.2.7 H: N disputes I's record through process p. Effective; one open dispute; content unchanged.
§11.2.7 I: two supersessions of R0 by I. Both forked; no latest supported state.
